key_insight: Language models can act as research world models that predict experiment outcomes, and their accuracy improves substantially when they are trained on real experimental research experience.
engineering_relevance: For AI research agents, this means fewer wasted trials and better experiment selection under tight compute budgets, improving efficiency in recursive self-improvement workflows.
method: Collected 2,600+ experimental records from 9 research environments spanning pretraining, post-training, and inference.
Evaluated language models on predicting outcomes and ranking candidate interventions as research world models.
Compared in-environment and cross-environment transfer, including multi-round Autoresearch under a fixed selection budget.
evidence_signal: The study covers more than 171,000 H100 GPU-hours, and research knowledge improved unseen-intervention prediction within the same environment by Spearman +0.27; cross-environment transfer reduced selection regret by 78% in one case.
watch_item: Performance depends on the availability and quality of prior experimental data, so gains may be weaker in new environments with little or no research history.
paper_title: Language Models as AI Research World Models
